settings.name_in_paper: Performative regret minimization with performative feedback (epsilon-sensitive distribution map)
unmapped: Performative feedback: after deploying theta the learner observes m_0 i.i.d. samples from the induced distribution D(theta) (strictly richer than bandit feedback) and knows the loss function l(z;theta), so it can estimate DPR(theta, theta') for all theta'
Distribution map is epsilon-sensitive (Wasserstein-1 Lipschitz with constant epsilon); loss is L_z-Lipschitz in z; loss arbitrary in theta (PR need not be Lipschitz or convex)
The learner knows the sensitivity epsilon, L_z, m_0 and an upper bound on the Rademacher complexity of the loss class
settings.definition_quote: At every time step $t$, the learner chooses a model $\theta_t$ and observes a constant number $m_0$ of i.i.d. samples, $\{z_t^{(i)}\}_{i\in{[m_0]}}, \text{ where } z_t^{(i)}\sim\cD(\theta_t)$. The regret incurred by choosing $\theta_t$ at time step $t$ is $\Delta(\theta_t):=\PR(\theta_t) - \PR(\thetaPO)$

settings.name_in_paper: Performative regret minimization for location families
unmapped: Performative feedback: learner observes m_0 samples z = z_0 + mu_*^T theta from D(theta) after deploying theta, and knows the loss l(z;theta)
Location family distribution map with unknown matrix mu_* in R^{d_Theta x m}, ||mu_*|| <= M_* known; base distribution D_0 zero-mean 1-subgaussian
The learner knows the base distribution D_0, the norm bound M_* and m_0
Loss l(z;theta) in [0,1], L_z-Lipschitz in z, arbitrary (possibly nonconvex) in theta
settings.definition_quote: location families are distribution maps of the form $z \sim \cD(\theta) \Leftrightarrow z \stackrel{d}{=} z_0 + \mu_*^\top \theta$, where  $\mu_*\in\mathbb{R}^{d_\Theta \times m}$ is an unknown matrix and $z_0\in\mathbb{R}^m$ is a zero-mean subgaussian sample from a base distribution $\cD_0$.

algorithms.name: Performative Regret Minimization for Location Families (LinUCB-inspired)

symbols.L_z: Lipschitz constant of the loss in z
symbols.eps_s: sensitivity epsilon of the distribution map (Wasserstein-1)
symbols.m_0: number of samples observed per deployment
symbols.C_rad: upper bound on the Rademacher complexity C*(l) of the loss class

conditions: loss l(z;theta) in [0,1] and L_z-Lipschitz in z
tuning: gamma_p = 2^-p, r_p = gamma_p/(L_z eps), n_p = ceil((2C+3sqrt(log T))^2/(gamma_p^2 m_0))

source.label: thm:fine-grained-seq
source.quote: Assume the loss $\ell(z;\theta)$ is $L_z$-Lipschitz in $z$ and let $\epsilon$ denote the sensitivity of the distribution map. Suppose that $\mathfrak{C}$ is any value such that $\mathfrak{C}^*(\ell) \leq \mathfrak{C}$ and $m_0 = o(\mathcal{B}_{\log T,\mathfrak{C}}^2)$... Then, after $T$ time steps, Algorithm~\ref{alg:adaptive-exploration} achieves a regret bound of $\Reg(T) = \cO(T^{\frac{d+1}{d+2}}(\frac{ (L_z \epsilon)^d \mathcal{B}_{\log T,\mathfrak{C}}^2}{m_0})^{\frac{1}{d+2}}  + \sqrt{T} \frac{\mathcal{B}_{\log T,\mathfrak{C}}}{\sqrt{m_0}} )$

results.notes: Performative regret defined via E PR(theta_t) - min PR, i.e. pseudo-regret. Theorem 1 (informal) restates this as O_tilde(sqrt(T) + T^{(d+1)/(d+2)}(L_z eps)^{d/(d+2)}).

symbols.L_z: Lipschitz constant of the loss in z
symbols.eps_s: sensitivity epsilon of the distribution map
symbols.C_rad: upper bound on Rademacher complexity of loss class

source.quote: if $T$ is sufficiently large, the final iterate $\theta_T$ of Algorithm~\ref{alg:adaptive-exploration} satisfies: $\E [\PR(\theta_T) - \min_{\theta \in \Theta} \PR(\theta)] \leq  \cO(T^{-\frac{1}{d+2}} (\frac{ (L_z \epsilon)^d \mathcal{B}_{\log T,\mathfrak{C}}^2}{m_0})^{\frac{1}{d+2}}  )$

results.notes: Suboptimality of final iterate, stated in a remark as an intermediate step of the proof; the setting's objective is cumulative regret.

symbols.L_z: Lipschitz constant of the loss in z
symbols.m_z: dimension m of the data z

conditions: loss L_z-Lipschitz in z and in [0,1]

source.label: thm:lin_bound
source.quote: Suppose that $\ell(z;\theta)$ is $L_z$-Lipschitz in $z$, $\cD_0$ is $1$-subgaussian, and $m_0 = o(\log T)$. Then, after $T$ time steps, Algorithm~\ref{alg:location-families} achieves a regret bound of $\Reg(T) = \tilde \cO  (\frac 1 {\sqrt{m_0}} \max\{L_z, 1\} \sqrt{T}\max\{d_\Theta,\sqrt{d_\Theta m}\})$.

cited_results.setting_description: Performative prediction cast as Lipschitz continuum-armed bandit with (L_theta + eps L_z)-Lipschitz PR, m_0 = o(log T); d is the (L_theta+eps L_z)-zooming dimension
